analysis.title: Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN): Framing Key Areas of Investor Focus Ahead of Holiday Shopping & AWS Re:Invent
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy and $370 12-month price target on AMZN, calling it the most compelling risk/reward in its mega/large cap coverage. AMZN is on the Goldman Sachs Americas Conviction List.

Alexa for Shopping (formerly Rufus) produced ~$12B of incremental revenue in 2025 per Amazon's Q4 call. GS projects ~$16B in 2026 (+33% YoY), using 400M users, a 16% conversion rate and ~$250 revenue per converted user.

GS argues Alexa for Shopping leaves AMZN positively exposed to agentic commerce, contrary to much investor sentiment. Shop Direct and Buy for Me let the agent surface and buy from merchants outside Amazon's marketplace without taking inventory.
Everyday Essentials and fresh grocery grew ~3x faster than the rest of Stores and are now ~50% of units sold, up from ~one-third in 1Q25. The mix shift lowers revenue per unit.
GS calculates Stores contribution profit contracted ~220bps YoY in 3Q because variable costs to serve do not fall with lower prices. Worldwide paid units grew +12% YoY in Q3 (+17% in Q2).

Paid units grew over 1pp faster than logistics costs in Q3, helped by regionalized inventory placement, shorter delivery distances and more consolidated shipments. Logistics costs have risen ~10 percentage points as a share of 1P and 3P revenue since 2019.

GS says efficiency gains in the network are larger than reported margins show, because Amazon reinvested part of the savings into faster delivery and automation. Amazon now runs more than 1 million robots in fulfillment.

GS forecasts North America and International EBIT margins (excluding Devices and Services losses) at ~17% by 2030, with ~21% possible under continued automation. A ~13% lower cost to serve per unit by 2030 equals ~250bps of upside to consolidated margins, ~80% in fulfillment and ~20% in COGS.

Amazon partnered with Uber Eats, giving U.S. Prime members $0 delivery on eligible $25+ restaurant orders across 10k cities, replacing the Grubhub+ arrangement. Uber Eats is also integrated into Alexa+.

AWS grew 39% YoY in 3Q26, below GS expectations. GS attributes this to capacity availability and compute timing. Management expects AWS growth of 40% or more in 2027 and 2028, and a $1tn AWS business in 5-10 years.
GS estimates AI services at ~16% of AWS revenue in 2026 (15.9%), growing at a triple-digit rate. AI run-rate revenue passed $15B in 1Q26 and $25B in 2Q26.

GS estimates AI services operating margin in the mid-20% range versus low-40% for core AWS. It expects AI margins to improve with utilization, Bedrock and Trainium, supporting a durable high-30s consolidated AWS margin.

GS's backlog conversion framework gives an illustrative upside case of AWS revenue growth of ~55.3% in 2027 and ~53.8% in 2028. GS says this is not its base case. Its base case is 40.0% in 2027 and 35.7% in 2028.

Management said it expects to begin selling Trainium externally exiting 2027. Third-party sales bring hardware revenue upfront, while internal deployment earns recurring compute revenue over a ~5-6 year chip life.

Investor focus at Re:Invent: Trainium next generation and external sales, customer diversification beyond frontier labs toward inference, Bedrock as the enterprise agent control plane, and core cloud differentiation.
GS's $370 SOTP target uses 14x EV/GAAP EBIT for North America, 1.3x EV/Sales for International and 27x EV/GAAP EBIT for AWS, on NTM+1 estimates. Downside case is $190 and upside case is $500.

market_movers.rationale: GS calls AMZN the most compelling risk/reward in its mega/large cap coverage and keeps it on the Americas Conviction List. The case rests on AWS growth of 40% or more in 2027-2028 and long-term retail margin upside from automation.

earnings_insights: AWS grew 39% YoY in 3Q26 (reported), below GS expectations.
Worldwide paid units grew +12% YoY in Q3 2026 (reported) versus +17% in Q2.
GS estimates Stores contribution profit contracted ~220bps YoY in 3Q26.
GS EPS estimates: $1.91 for 9/26E, $2.29 for 12/26E and $2.36 for 3/27E. Full-year EPS estimates are $12.67 for 12/26E, $11.18 for 12/27E and $14.81 for 12/28E.
Management said on the 3Q26 call that retail is now a double-digit operating margin business including advertising.

trade_ideas.description: Long AMZN, Buy rating with $370 12-month price target (43.8% upside from $257.37)
trade_ideas.rationale: AWS acceleration driven by AI workloads, Trainium and Bedrock, plus long-term retail margin upside from automation and a growing agentic commerce position.
trade_ideas.risk: Competition in eCommerce or cloud, failure to scale high-margin businesses such as advertising, cloud, third-party selling and subscriptions, and investment-driven margin pressure.

risk_factors: Competition affecting eCommerce or cloud growth
Lack of success scaling high-margin businesses including advertising, cloud, third-party selling and subscriptions
Investments across initiatives creating a headwind to gross or operating margin
Product or platform changes needed to comply with global regulation
Global macro volatility and investor risk appetite for growth stocks
Near-term retail margin pressure from lower-ASP grocery and Everyday Essentials mix and faster delivery costs
AWS growth subject to capacity availability and timing of compute coming online
charts_described: Exhibit 1 builds Alexa for Shopping revenue from users (300m in 2025, 400m in 2026), 16% conversion versus 10% typical, and $250 revenue per converted user, reaching $12,000m in 2025 and $16,000m in 2026.
Exhibit 4 shows North America Everyday Essentials and Grocery at 50% of US units, growing ~3x faster than other categories.
Exhibit 12 shows North America and International EBIT margin excluding D&S losses reaching ~17% by 2030E, and ~21% with automation.
Exhibit 15 shows AWS revenue of $177,037m in 2026E, $247,897m in 2027E and $336,370m in 2028E, with AI services at 15.9%, 27.2% and 40.7% of AWS revenue.
Exhibit 17 shows an AWS year-end backlog of $578,000m in 2026E and an upside AWS revenue case of $274,977m in 2027E and $422,822m in 2028E versus GS base case of $247,897m and $336,370m.

tension_points.bull_case: Alexa for Shopping, with 400M users and a 16% conversion rate, keeps the discovery-to-purchase funnel inside Amazon. GS projects ~$16bn of incremental revenue in 2026.
tension_points.bear_case: Much investor sentiment sees third-party LLM shopping agents as a threat to Amazon's commerce traffic, which GS says it heard in client discussions.

tension_points.bull_case: Lower cost to serve, robotics and automation could lift North America and International EBIT margins from ~17% to ~21% by 2030, and the grocery halo effect raises customer lifetime value.
tension_points.bear_case: Grocery and Everyday Essentials mix and faster delivery cut Stores contribution profit by ~220bps YoY in 3Q and lower revenue per unit.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Paid unit growth failing to keep outpacing logistics cost growth, which GS tracks in Exhibit 10.

tension_points.bull_case: Management expects 40% or more growth in 2027 and 2028, and GS's illustrative backlog conversion case reaches ~54-55%.
tension_points.bear_case: AWS grew 39% in 3Q26, below GS expectations, and growth is gated by capacity availability and compute timing.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AWS growth below the 40% management framing as capacity comes online.

theme_stances.key_argument: Management's 40% or more growth framing for 2027-2028, backlog conversion and rising Bedrock and Trainium contribution point to an AWS estimate revision cycle investors underappreciate.
theme_stances.evidence: early innings of an AWS estimate revision cycle that remains underappreciated by investors

theme_stances.key_argument: Alexa for Shopping keeps Amazon in control of the customer relationship, product data and transaction as shopping shifts toward AI agents.
theme_stances.evidence: contrary to much investor sentiment based on our discussion

theme_stances.key_argument: Near-term pressure from grocery mix and fast delivery is offset by lower cost to serve from robotics, regionalization and automation.
